title: HTTP/2 frame
summary: Every HTTP/2 connection is a sequence of frames. Each frame has a 9-byte header (length 24 bits, type 8 bits, flags 8 bits, R 1 bit + stream id 31 bits) followed by a payload of `length` bytes.

ext.summary: Every HTTP/2 connection is a sequence of frames. Each frame has a 9-byte header (length 24 bits, type 8 bits, flags 8 bits, R 1 bit + stream id 31 bits) followed by a payload of `length` bytes.

structure.meaning: Payload length in octets (max 2^14 default, up to 2^24-1 with SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE).
Frame type (DATA=0x00, HEADERS=0x01, PRIORITY=0x02, RST_STREAM=0x03, SETTINGS=0x04, PUSH_PROMISE=0x05, PING=0x06, GOAWAY=0x07, WINDOW_UPDATE=0x08, CONTINUATION=0x09).
Type-specific flags (END_STREAM, END_HEADERS, PADDED, PRIORITY, ACK, ...).
Reserved bit (must be 0) + 31-bit stream id (0 for connection-level frames).

ext.example_decoded: SETTINGS frame, stream 0, no flags, empty payload
notes: Frame header is always exactly 9 bytes.
Maximum frame size defaults to 16384 octets; negotiated via SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE.
Stream id 0 is the connection; odd ids are client-initiated, even are server-initiated (push).
HPACK (RFC 7541) compresses headers into HEADERS/CONTINUATION payloads.
